prompt_en: A cinematic yet documentary photograph inside a small radio telescope control cabin during a dusk power test. One fictional adult stands beside a waist-high brushed-metal console, with visible adult face and hair appearance guided by the attached portrait: a soft oval face, dark eyes, and a short dark bob with loose wispy bangs. The adult wears a charcoal utility overshirt over a plain crewneck. Their right hand grips and turns a large red knurled power selector on the near edge of the console, with the wrist, forearm, elbow, and shoulder forming a relaxed reachable chain. Their left palm holds a paper checklist flat on the console beside the selector; both hands, the paper, and the selector are fully visible in the same frame. A short row of amber status lamps illuminates in sequence above the turned selector while the adult glances down at the readings, face in clear three-quarter view. Beyond the cabin window, the pale curved structure of a radio dish rises against a violet blue evening sky. Reflections of the amber lamps appear faintly on the window glass while the exterior dish stays readable through it. A cool dusk glow shapes the face and hair, and warm console light falls locally on the fingertips, red selector, and worn metal surface. At console height, a normal-lens medium portrait places the adult slightly left of center, and the radio dish rises through the right half of the framed window. The matte charcoal console surround carries broad subdued shading; its brushed-steel rim catches one narrow glint, while adjacent window glass keeps a faint amber interior reflection over the transmitted dish. Cool window light colors the adult's window-side sleeve, warm console light colors the paper and fingertips, and the two source-bound zones meet softly along the forearm. The eyes, both hands, and red selector stay crisp; intermediate meter faces remain readable, while the far dish loses only its finest detail. The red selector's ridges show small polished wear where fingers grip them; neighboring unhandled coating remains comparatively intact and the selector keeps a solid continuous form. These depth and material cues belong to one coherent cabin exposure.
